newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lankan Newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lankan Newspapers - July 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
TAMIL PARITES ASKED TO SUPPORT DEVOLUTION PACKAGE

Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, who was in Sri Lanka last week, asked the Tamil and Moslem parties to support the ruling People's Alliance's (PA) proposals to give more power to minorities. He said Australia was backing the devolution package, aimed at ending the 14-year-old ethnic crisis.
THE ISLAND
NURSE SHORTAGE AFFECTS NATIONAL HOSPITAL

A shortage of nurses has led to a fall in the number of surgical operations at Colombo's National Hospital. There are 459 unfilled vacancies for nurses, which constitutes 24 percent of their total strength.
DIVAINA
AUSTRALIA DEPORTS 15 SRI LANKANS
Fifteen Sri Lankans who entered Australia illegally and were deported by Australian authorities, were arrested by police on arrival in Colombo on Saturday.
VIRAKESARI & THINAKKURUL
MINISTER TO ADDRESS FEARS ON NEW ELECTORAL SYSTEM

The Minister of Constitutional Affairs Gamini Peiris and officials of his ministry will meet Tamil leaders on Monday to discuss proposed changes to the electoral system. Tamil parites have expressed fears that the changes would adversely affect minority representation and the strength of minority parties in parliament.
VIRAKESARI
INDO-SRI LANKA AGREEMENT CENTENARY CONFERENCE IN GENEVA
A conference to review the Indo-Sri Lanka Agreement, provincial councils and talks between the present government and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam is scheduled to start on Monday in Geneva.
The conference which has been arranged by Alert International would continue for three days.
POLITICAL
LANKADEEPA & VIRSKESARI
LEFTIST PARTY TO QUIT CABINET POSTS

The leftist Lanka Sama Samaj Party (LSS), a member of the ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition government, will ask its members to resign from their cabinet posts as a protest against some unilateral decisions taken by the Sri Lanka Freedom party, the largest party in the PA.
A LSSP spokesman however said the party would continue to be part of the PA.
